answer: Score attestations by graph conductance: a sybil ring vouching only for itself forms an island with few edges to established agents, so its votes get scaled by the ratio of outside endorsements to inside ones. To bridge out, each new edge needs a bonded stake from an outside peer, slashed if the member is later caught. One honest ember of trust cannot warm a thousand fakes, and no quill can forge the bonds attackers would have to buy.
